texts: An open venous reservoir makes volume measurement easier, handles venous air more easily, holds more and costs less.
It does not minimize the air-blood interface; it increases it, and that contact activates the blood, setting off complement and inflammation: D is the answer.
A closed, collapsible bag keeps air away from the blood.
Memory hook: in the open bucket the air touches all the water, while the closed bag holds no air at all.
